_comment: Short answers to common questions about ImpactMojo, shown as the Answers group at the top of site search (js/search.js). This replaces the answer bank of the retired Mojini chat assistant (js/faq-bank.js). Each entry: q is the question as a reader would ask it, keywords are the words they might type, a is the answer in plain text (root-relative /...html paths and https links in it become links), url is the page to open. Counts written here are checked by scripts/check-counts.py.

answers.a: Every signed-up learner gets a free certificate of completion for each course they finish. It appears in your account and carries an ID that anyone can check on /verify-certificate.html. Practitioner members and above can also download it as a PDF. It records completion and carries no academic credit.
answers.label: Verify a certificate

answers.a: A certificate of completion is free. A certificate of assessment is the separate Assessed Credential, at Rs 2,499, which adds a verified credential to a free pathway.
answers.label: Assessed Credential

answers.a: ImpactMojo is a practitioner-focused learning platform. It is not an accredited degree programme and does not award academic credit.
answers.label: About ImpactMojo

answers.q: Can I show my work in a portfolio?
answers.a: The work you make in the Studios and Practice Packs is yours to show: a Theory of Change, a sampling design, a policy brief. Practitioner members also get a public portfolio page.
answers.label: Portfolio

answers.a: The courses, Studios and games are free. Membership has two paid plans for individuals, Practitioner at Rs 399 a month and Professional at Rs 999 a month, and a Team plan for organisations. The paid plans add exports, the full Practice Packs and other extras. See /premium.html for what each plan includes.
answers.label: Membership plans

answers.a: Practitioner (Rs 399 a month) opens all 18 Practice Packs in full, export from the Research Question Builder, the ToR Builder and four Studios, and a public portfolio page. Professional (Rs 999 a month) adds export from the Qualitative Insights Lab, the Statistical Code Converter, the Logframe Builder, the Empathy Map and the AI Strategy Canvas, code from the Visualization Cookbook, the DevEconomics Toolkit and priority coaching. The Team plan (Rs 1,499 per user per month) gives every member Professional access and adds a team dashboard.
answers.label: Membership plans

answers.a: The refund policy sets out when a payment can be refunded and how to ask for it.
answers.label: Refund policy

answers.a: There are 22 flagship courses and 84 foundational courses, 106 in all, plus 15 Code School courses. The catalogue lists every one of them.
answers.label: Course catalogue

answers.a: Start with any 101 course. They are beginner-friendly decks that focus on practical understanding.
answers.label: 101 courses

answers.q: How long does a course take?
answers.a: Courses are self-paced, so the time depends on you. Each course page lists its modules. When a live or cohort option is offered, the course page says so.
answers.label: Course catalogue

answers.a: Most of the site opens without signing in. A free account saves your progress and gives you a certificate when you finish a course.
answers.label: Create a free account

answers.a: Use the reset page to get a link by email, then choose a new password.
answers.label: Reset your password

answers.a: There are 35 Studios (also called Labs): browser-based tools you work through yourself, such as the Theory of Change Studio and the MEL Studio. They open in your browser with nothing to install.
answers.label: All Studios

answers.a: There are 135 games, 18 simulations and the rest short puzzles, that let you try an idea from a course by playing it.
answers.label: Game library

answers.q: Can I learn R, Python or Stata here?
answers.a: Yes, in Code School. R, Python, SQL, the tidyverse, pandas and Shiny run in your browser with nothing to install. Guided courses cover Stata, SPSS, Power BI, jamovi and JASP, OpenRefine, QGIS, KoboToolbox and ODK, spreadsheets, and Git with Quarto.
answers.label: Code School

answers.a: The Data Room holds 21 data explorers: interactive pages built on India's official surveys, the Union Budget, administrative records and open academic data, from ASER and NFHS to prisons, CSR and air quality. The newest is the Travel Survey Explorer at /nhts.html.
answers.label: All explorers

answers.q: Where can I find datasets to practise with?
answers.a: The Dataverse lists 343 curated data sources. DevData Practice is free to use and generates synthetic datasets in the style of household surveys, trials and labour force surveys for practising analysis. None of it is real survey data.
answers.label: Dataverse

answers.a: There are 192 reading companions: interactive guides to books on development, economics and social change.
answers.label: Reading companions

answers.a: ImpactLex is a searchable glossary of more than 490 development terms, acronyms and formulas. Each entry says how it was written and whether it has been reviewed.
answers.label: ImpactLex

answers.q: Where can I find case studies?
answers.a: FieldCases is a free, searchable library of more than 200 cited development case studies, each with its sources listed, at https://varnasr.github.io/dev-case-studies/
answers.label: FieldCases

answers.q: Where can I find research papers?
answers.a: Development Discourses is a curated open-access library of more than 600 research papers, books and grey literature on development and public policy, sorted by topic, at https://devdiscourses.impactmojo.in/ Every resource is open access.
answers.label: Development Discourses

answers.q: Can I transcribe interviews in Indian languages?
answers.a: VaniScribe transcribes field interviews and recordings in the browser in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu and other Indian languages, using your own Sarvam AI key, so it is free to try. The Professional Colab notebook adds speaker labels and longer interviews.
answers.label: VaniScribe

answers.q: Is the site available in Hindi or other languages?
answers.a: Content is in English. The home, About and Books pages and the site menus can be switched into Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil and Telugu. Those translations are produced by machine and may contain errors. Course content is in English only.
answers.label: About ImpactMojo

answers.q: Does it work on a phone?
answers.a: ImpactMojo works in any modern browser on a computer or a phone. Pages you have opened before also work offline.
answers.label: Accessibility

answers.a: Every page is audited daily against WCAG 2.1 AA in light and dark themes. The accessibility statement explains how to report a barrier.
answers.label: Accessibility statement

answers.q: What do you do with my data?
answers.a: The privacy policy explains what is collected, why, and how to ask for your data to be corrected or deleted.
answers.label: Privacy policy

answers.a: Write to hello@impactmojo.in or use the form on /contact.html. Known problems are listed on /known-issues.html.
answers.label: Contact

answers.a: Yes. Send the topic and what you would want to learn from it through the contact form.
answers.label: Contact

answers.a: Dojos are 90-minute practice sessions that build practitioner skills through doing. There are 56 sessions in the series, at Rs 1,500 per session in Delhi, Bangalore or online.
answers.label: Dojos

answers.q: Do you run workshops for organisations?
answers.a: Three-day workshops for NGOs and development teams start at Rs 12,000 for up to 6 participants. The Workshops page has the topics, dates and booking form.
answers.label: Workshops

answers.a: Coaching is one-on-one or in small groups. The Coaching page lists the coaches, topics and how to book.
answers.label: Coaching

answers.q: Can my team or organisation use ImpactMojo?
answers.a: Yes. Courses build shared foundations and Studios help teams design and improve programmes. The Team plan adds a team dashboard and custom learning paths.
answers.label: Team plan

answers.q: Can I use ImpactMojo in my teaching?
answers.a: Yes. The teaching page explains how to use courses and Studios in a class, and /lms-export.html packages a course for your LMS.
answers.label: Teach with ImpactMojo

answers.q: Is there a community I can join?
answers.a: The WhatsApp Professional Learning Community connects practitioners, researchers and changemakers across South Asia to share resources and discuss fieldwork. The community page has the link to join.
answers.label: Community

answers.a: ImpactMojo was founded by Dr. Varna Sri Raman and Vandana Soni and is supported by PinPoint Ventures.
answers.label: About ImpactMojo

answers.q: Is there a power calculator or DiD simulator?
answers.a: The DevEconomics Toolkit is a set of 11 interactive Shiny apps: an RCT power calculator, a DiD simulator, an RDD explorer, a synthetic control visualiser, a Gini and Lorenz curve tool and more. It is part of the Professional plan.
answers.label: Membership plans

answers.a: The Visualization Cookbook has 63 chart recipes with Python code, organised by the question you are asking of your data. Browsing is free and copying the code needs a Professional plan.
answers.label: Visualization Cookbook
